NVIDIA CAP: absent env means ordinary capacity open. Present env must match /^(0|[1-9][0-9]*)$/ and Number(value) must be a safe integer; malformed is unavailable. completion.text: {"accepted":false,"summary":"The bounded design is substantially sound across its declared test surface: workspace isolation, semantic gating, cap validation, and persistence all pass their stated suites, and the three prior review residues (Groq schema failure, NVIDIA metadata repetition, Gemini misreads) are correctly resolved or accepted. Two concrete residual defects remain material. First, the NVIDIA cap exhaustion check (exchange count >= cap) is not described as atomic; under concurrent inference requests, two callers can both observe count < cap, both proceed, and both increment, yielding final count exceeding cap by the concurrency factor. The 13-vector suite covers only single-threaded boundary shapes. Second, the fresh-route majority predicate over reviewers is undefined when review empties the eligible pool; a vacuously-true evaluation would admit a change with zero reviews, and this edge is not listed among the 9 covered review-suite vectors. A third lower-severity asymmetry exists between the protected route's 'at least one' fresh acceptance and the fresh route's majority requirement, but this may be intentional given the capsule's prior validation burden. No file-mutation, execution, integration, or customer-acceptance claims are made.","findings":[{"severity":"medium","area":"NVIDIA cap — concurrent exhaustion","problem":"The cap check (exchange count >= cap) and the subsequent increment are two separate steps. Under concurrent inference requests, multiple callers can pass the predicate before any increment lands, allowing the realised exchange count to exceed the declared cap by the degree of concurrency.","evidence":"The 13-vector suite covers text, fraction, negative, hex, whitespace, leading-zero, unsafe-integer, zero/exhausted, open, and unset — all single-threaded boundary shapes. No concurrent-increment vector is described or implied.","recommendation":"Gate cap consumption behind an atomic compare-and-increment (e.g., an atomic counter, a mutex-protected read-modify-write, or a single-writer queue). Alternatively enforce the cap at the scheduler level before any exchange is dispatched."},{"severity":"medium","area":"Semantic acceptance — empty reviewer pool","problem":"The fresh route requires 'a majority of unique reviewers.' If review empties the eligible set, the majority predicate is undefined; a vacuously-true evaluation admits the change with zero reviews, defeating the gate entirely.","evidence":"Nine review-suite vectors are described as passing, but the degenerate empty-pool case is not listed among them. The description does not state a fail-closed guard when eligible count is zero.","recommendation":"Assert eligible reviewer count >= 1 (or a configured minimum) before evaluating the majority predicate, and fail closed when the pool is empty. Add a dedicated zero-pool vector to the review suite."},{"severity":"low","area":"Semantic acceptance — protected route fresh-review gate asymmetry","problem":"The protected route requires 'at least one' fresh evidence-bound accepted review; the fresh route requires a majority. With a two-reviewer pool, one acceptance satisfies the protected gate but not necessarily the spirit of independent majority review, creating a weaker ongoing review requirement on the stronger protection path.","evidence":"Context states: 'Fresh route accepts only a majority of unique reviewers. Protected route … requires … at least one fresh evidence-bound accepted review.' No reviewer-pool floor is declared.","recommendation":"Clarify whether 'at least one' is intentionally weaker because the capsule supplies prior validation, or whether it should match the majority threshold. If intentional, document the rationale so a future reviewer does not tighten it incorrectly."}]}
